newsitem.title: INDIA: DELHI SHARES FIRM IN MID-SESSION TRADING.
newsitem.headline: DELHI SHARES FIRM IN MID-SESSION TRADING.

text.p: Delhi shares quoted higher in mid-session trade on Tuesday on speculative and investor buying on hopes that a more liberal carry-forward system will be introduced in Indian bourses soon, brokers said.
They said the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the market regulator, might announce an easier carry-forward system as recommended by an official committee.
A SEBI news conference is scheduled at 5.00 p.m (1130 GMT) on Tuesday.
Brokers said hectic trading took place in the shares of Reliance Industries Ltd, the State Bank of India (SBI), Tata Steel (Tisco) and ITC Ltd.
At 0700 GMT the benchmark index was up 2.10 points at 947.87.
"Players are cornering heavily-weighted speculative counters on hopes of sharp upsurge in their prices," said S.C. Juneja of the stock broking firm Jaico Credit Pvt Ltd.
Reliance moved up to 384.75 rupees but profit-taking pruned the early gains and the share was quoted at 382.20 rupees against the last close of 381.20.
Tisco shares gained 0.50 rupee to 216.20 rupees and the SBI 0.30 rupee to 333.75 rupees after rising to 335.95 rupees.

Hindustan Lever moved up six rupees to 1,536 rupees and Nestle India two rupees to 298 rupees. ITC was up 0.60 rupees at 579 rupees. Hero Honda rose 12 rupees to 598 and MTNL by one rupee to 290.30 rupees.
